Source. Inside the witness's `abstracts` block, the parser stores a scalar entry with key `hilight` and the quoted backslash string as its value. The missing `=` and trailing `;` only trigger warnings, so the malformed entry still materializes.

The parsed `hilight` entry is copied into the theme's abstract hash and replaces any older definition with the same key, so subsequent abstract expansion resolves `hilight` through attacker-controlled bytes.

During default-format expansion, when any built-in format containing `{hilight ...}` is processed, this code extracts the abstract name `hilight` from the format string and replaces it with the attacker-controlled value from `theme->abstracts`.

The built-in format's argument text is collected and the attacker-controlled abstract template is interpreted into a heap string `ret`. On the crashing witness this `ret` buffer ends in a single trailing backslash, which is exactly the case the fix's added `p[1] != '\0'` guard excludes.

Root cause. Because the current byte is the terminal backslash from step 4, this branch still executes even though no escaped character follows. `p++` advances to the NUL terminator, `expand_escape(&p)` leaves `p` there, and the code stays on the escape-decoding path that should have been rejected.
After step 5 has already advanced `p` onto the terminator for the final backslash case, the unconditional loop-end increment moves `p` one byte past the end of the `ret` allocation.
Sink. The next loop-condition dereference reads `*p` after step 6 moved the pointer one byte past the heap string, producing the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.
